stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The committee ___ every Tuesday to review the budget.
explanation: Rule: subject-verb agreement with a collective noun. 'Committee' is a singular collective noun, so it takes the singular verb 'meets'. 'Meet' is plural, and 'meeting'/'to meet' are non-finite forms that cannot serve as the main verb here.
hint: Is 'committee' one group acting as a unit? Then the verb should be singular, like 'it meets'.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Each of the players ___ a new uniform this season.
explanation: Rule: indefinite pronouns. 'Each' is always singular, so it takes the singular verb 'receives'. The plural-sounding phrase 'of the players' does not change the singular subject.
hint: Cross out 'of the players' — what is left? 'Each ___ a new uniform.'
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The books on the shelf ___ dusted every week.
explanation: Rule: the verb agrees with the subject, not with words in a prepositional phrase. The subject is the plural 'books' (not 'shelf'), so the plural verb 'are' is correct.
hint: Find the real subject — ignore 'on the shelf'. Books: one or many?
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Neither the coach nor the players ___ the change in schedule.
explanation: Rule: with 'neither/nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Players' (plural) is nearer the verb than 'coach', so the plural verb 'like' is correct.
hint: In a 'neither/nor' sentence, look at the subject closest to the blank.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? There ___ two good reasons to arrive early.
explanation: Rule: with 'there', the verb agrees with the true subject that follows it. 'Two good reasons' is plural, so the plural verb 'are' is correct.
hint: Flip the sentence: 'Two good reasons ___ there.' Now which verb fits?
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The team ___ its first championship in 2019.
explanation: Rule: the singular collective noun 'team' takes a singular verb, and the time marker 'in 2019' requires the past tense — 'won'. 'Wins' is singular but present tense, which conflicts with 2019.
hint: Two checks: is the subject singular? And what year is the sentence about?
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Every student and teacher ___ invited to the ceremony.
explanation: Rule: 'every' makes the subject singular even when it joins two nouns. 'Every student and teacher' is treated as singular, so 'was' is correct.
hint: 'Every' is a singular word — it forces the verb to be singular too.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The flock of birds ___ south each autumn.
explanation: Rule: collective nouns. 'Flock' is a singular collective noun acting as one unit, so it takes the singular verb 'migrates'. The plural 'birds' inside the prepositional phrase does not govern the verb.
hint: Is it one flock or many flocks moving? The subject is 'flock'.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Mathematics ___ my favorite subject.
explanation: Rule: subjects ending in -ics (mathematics, physics, economics) are singular despite the 's'. The singular verb 'is' is correct.
hint: Say it aloud: 'Mathematics is...' or 'Mathematics are...'? Trust your ear here.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The children in the park ___ loudly every evening.
explanation: Rule: plural subject takes a plural verb. 'Children' is plural, so 'play' is correct. Ignore the prepositional phrase 'in the park'.
hint: One child plays; many children ___?
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? A basket of fresh oranges ___ on the kitchen table.
explanation: Rule: the verb agrees with the subject 'basket' (singular), not with 'oranges' in the prepositional phrase. The singular verb 'sits' is correct.
hint: Cross out 'of fresh oranges' — 'A basket ___ on the table.'
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Either Maya or her sisters ___ bringing dessert.
explanation: Rule: with 'either/or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Sisters' (plural) is nearer the verb, so 'are' is correct.
hint: Look at the noun closest to the blank — 'Maya' or 'sisters'?
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The news about the storm ___ everyone worried.
explanation: Rule: 'news' is an uncountable noun and always singular, so the singular verb 'has' is correct — even though it ends in 's'.
hint: 'News' looks plural but behaves as one thing: 'the news has...'
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Ten dollars ___ enough for a simple lunch.
explanation: Rule: amounts of money, time, and distance are treated as singular units. 'Ten dollars' is one amount, so the singular verb 'is' is correct.
hint: Think of it as one price tag, not ten separate bills.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The paintings on the wall ___ by a local artist.
explanation: Rule: the subject is the plural 'paintings', so the plural verb 'were' is correct. 'On the wall' is just a prepositional phrase — it cannot change the subject's number.
hint: Remove 'on the wall' and read it: 'The paintings ___ by a local artist.'
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Someone ___ left a jacket in the classroom.
explanation: Rule: indefinite pronouns like 'someone', 'anyone', and 'nobody' are always singular. 'Someone has' is correct.
hint: 'Someone' means one unnamed person — singular.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The dog and the cat ___ in the backyard.
explanation: Rule: two subjects joined by 'and' form a plural subject. 'The dog and the cat' is plural, so 'play' is correct.
hint: And = plus. Two animals = plural verb.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Neither of the answers ___ correct.
explanation: Rule: 'neither' is always singular ('not one and not the other'), so the singular verb 'is' is correct.
hint: 'Neither' means zero of them — think singular.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The list of ingredients ___ on the fridge.
explanation: Rule: the subject is the singular 'list'; 'of ingredients' is a prepositional phrase that cannot change the verb. 'Is' is correct.
hint: The subject is 'list', not 'ingredients'.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Each book and magazine ___ a due-date stamp.
explanation: Rule: 'each' is singular no matter how many nouns follow it. 'Each book and magazine' takes the singular verb 'has'.
hint: 'Each' is the key word — it always pairs with a singular verb.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The flowers in the garden ___ beautiful in spring.
explanation: Rule: the plural subject 'flowers' takes the plural verb 'are'. Ignore 'in the garden'.
hint: One flower is beautiful; many flowers ___ beautiful?
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Nobody ___ the answer to that riddle.
explanation: Rule: 'nobody' is a singular indefinite pronoun, so it takes the singular verb 'knows'.
hint: 'Nobody' = not one person. Singular verb.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The number of students in the class ___ growing.
explanation: Rule: 'the number of' is singular (it refers to one figure), so 'is' is correct. Contrast with 'a number of', which is plural.
hint: 'The number' = one number. One number is singular.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? A number of students ___ volunteered for the event.
explanation: Rule: 'a number of' means 'several' and is plural, so the plural verb 'have' is correct. Contrast with 'the number of', which is singular.
hint: 'A number of students' really means 'several students' — plural.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The jury ___ its verdict yesterday.
explanation: Rule: 'jury' is a singular collective noun acting as one unit, and 'yesterday' requires past tense — 'reached'.
hint: One jury, one verdict, yesterday = singular past.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Bread and butter ___ a simple breakfast.
explanation: Rule: when two nouns joined by 'and' name one single item or idea, the verb is singular. 'Bread and butter' as one breakfast takes 'is'.
hint: Here bread-and-butter is one dish, not two separate things.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The stars ___ brightly tonight.
explanation: Rule: the plural subject 'stars' takes the plural verb 'shine'. In the present tense, plural verbs do not end in 's'.
hint: Present tense: singular adds -s ('shines'), plural drops it ('shine').
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? One of my friends ___ in Chicago.
explanation: Rule: the subject is the singular 'one', not 'friends' in the prepositional phrase. 'One ... lives' is correct.
hint: The subject is 'one'. 'One of my friends lives' — the 's' verb matches 'one'.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The teacher, along with her students, ___ the museum.
explanation: Rule: phrases like 'along with', 'as well as', and 'together with' do not change the subject's number. The singular 'teacher' takes 'visits'.
hint: 'Along with her students' is extra information — the subject is still 'teacher'.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Scissors ___ used to cut paper.
explanation: Rule: nouns that name tools in two parts (scissors, glasses, trousers) are always plural. 'Scissors are' is correct.
hint: Two blades = plural, always.
source: Original question authored for Unschool Academy; rule aligned to College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing — Standard English Conventions: subject-verb agreement (satsuite.collegeboard.org). Level L1 (Foundation).
